profile.reading: This building sits within the footprint of the former Loring Air Force Base in Limestone, Maine, now redeveloped as the Loring Commerce Centre, a roughly 3,800 acre commercial, industrial, and aviation park built from the decommissioned base's own buildings and infrastructure. The generic name attached to this listing, simply Datacenter, gives no operator or company identity of its own. The Commerce Centre's published tenant directory lists more than twenty businesses on site, including one technology firm, Lattice Technology Group, an engineering and systems integration consultancy, but Lattice's own description of its work is consulting and architecture design rather than operating server infrastructure or leasing hosting space, and nothing ties that company specifically to this building. Former military bases like Loring often retain purpose built communications or computer rooms from their active service days, structures that sometimes continue in some IT or utility role for a redeveloped site even without becoming a commercial data center business. Given the bare generic tag and the lack of any confirmed operator name tied to this specific structure, this entry is recorded as an unconfirmed building within the Loring Commerce Centre redevelopment, most plausibly a legacy base facility repurposed for some internal IT or utility function, rather than a verified commercial data center.

reading.body:
This entry is an unconfirmed facility. The building sits on the grounds of Loring Commerce Centre, a 3,800-acre redevelopment of Loring Air Force Base in Limestone, Maine, but carries only the generic name "Datacenter" with no operator identity published. Research exhausted all available leads: the Commerce Centre's business directory lists over twenty tenants but confirms no data center operator; only Lattice Technology Group, a systems integration consultancy, appears tech-adjacent, with no confirmed ties to this specific structure.

No specifications are published for this facility. The building most plausibly represents a legacy infrastructure structure from the former military base, repurposed for internal IT or utility functions within the industrial park rather than commercial hosting or colocation. Without power consumption, rack density, cooling capacity, or operator confirmation in any public source, no capacity figure can be assigned.

This campus cannot be ranked against peers. Maine has three mapped data center facilities in aggregate, zero with published power specifications, and a state total of zero published megawatts of confirmed capacity. The absence of data does not indicate absence of infrastructure, only absence of disclosure.
